extracted.intended_audience: consumer PR professionals, brand marketers, communications teams, and agencies
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating or designing consumer PR campaigns—especially those that reference social issues—so they avoid tone-deaf messaging, cultural harm, and public backlash. The rubric focuses on cultural sensitivity, authenticity, representation, crisis response, and stakeholder involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: When brands attempt to address social issues in their PR campaigns, they must do so with an understanding of the history, pain, and significance of the movements they are referencing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don’t treat movements as marketing props. Research historical context, consult subject-matter experts, and ensure messaging acknowledges real grievances and trauma. Anti-pattern: reducing movements to a feel-good backdrop for product imagery (as the Pepsi ad did).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentic engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize authentic engagement with the causes they wish to support. Authenticity is key to ensuring that PR campaigns resonate and do not come across as exploitative or opportunistic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate sustained commitment (actions, partnerships, funding), not one-off slogans. Look for long-term programmatic alignment rather than fleeting campaign tie-ins. Example positive action: supporting organizations doing the work rather than only using their imagery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid performative or insincere activism
rubrics_metrics.description: If a brand does not have a genuine commitment to social justice, it risks being perceived as 'performative' or 'insincere'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess internal policies, past behavior, and resource commitments before claiming alignment with a cause. Signals of insincerity include using activism language without follow-through or switching causes opportunistically for sales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate representation and spokesperson selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Brands need to be careful about who they choose to represent their messaging; casting privileged figures with little connection to the struggles depicted can reinforce perception of being out of touch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer spokespeople with authentic ties to the issue or include voices from affected communities. Anti-pattern: centering celebrities as 'heroes' of movements they don’t belong to (the Pepsi example casting Kendall Jenner).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not trivialize complex issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid reducing complex social justice movements to a momentary, consumer-friendly slogan or suggesting simple consumer actions are solutions to systemic problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure campaign messaging reflects the complexity of the issue and does not imply that buying or using a product equates to meaningful change. Test for messaging that oversimplifies root causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid co-opting protest imagery for commercial gain
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use the imagery of protests and activism purely to sell a product without acknowledging the real pain and struggle involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using protest motifs, secure consent, involve organizers, and avoid framing commercial products as conflict-resolution tools. Anti-pattern: depicting a can-of-soda as resolving police–protester tension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate and test for social media backlash
rubrics_metrics.description: Social media users can rapidly identify problematic elements and amplify criticism; campaigns must anticipate potential reactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-test concepts with diverse focus groups and do digital social listening simulations to identify triggers. Plan for how a message could be reframed by audiences and have mitigation strategies ready.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely, sincere crisis response and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: When missteps occur, brands must respond quickly and sincerely; Pepsi pulled the ad and issued a public apology after the backlash.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apologies should acknowledge harm, outline concrete corrective steps, and avoid defensive language. Note: a swift apology may not fully undo reputational damage—follow-up actions are essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align campaigns with brand values and avoid opportunism
rubrics_metrics.description: Campaigns should reflect genuine alignment with the brand’s values; attempting to capitalize on movements for commercial gain risks reputational harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit whether the campaign’s values and the brand’s track record match. Avoid jumping on social movements solely because they are topical or trend-driven.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use platform to encourage reflection, not spectacle
rubrics_metrics.description: Brands should aim to encourage critical reflection or understanding rather than turning serious issues into spectacle or entertainment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft content that educates, highlights voices of those affected, and promotes constructive action instead of staging feel-good moments that downplay seriousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Involve stakeholders and affected communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies should involve real activists, communities, and stakeholders when addressing issues related to social justice to ensure messaging comes from a place of respect and understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Co-create content, secure endorsements, and offer platform and resources to stakeholders. Treat involvement as meaningful collaboration, not token consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect lived experiences of marginalized groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid narratives that marginalize or erase the voices and experiences of the people whose struggles the campaign references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Center lived experiences in storytelling, give voice to those directly impacted, and avoid speaking over or replacing those voices with privileged perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid savior narratives and centering privileged 'heroes'
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not frame privileged figures as rescuers of marginalized communities; this reinforces problematic power dynamics and tone-deafness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure narratives recognize agency of affected communities and avoid plots where an outsider resolves systemic injustice through a single act (e.g., handing over a product).

rubrics_metrics.name: Match tone and gravity to the issue (avoid tone-deaf communication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tone must be appropriate to the subject matter; tone-deaf communication can turn well-intended campaigns into PR disasters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review tone with diverse internal and external reviewers, avoid flippant or trivializing language/images for serious topics, and prioritize empathy over trendiness.
